verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:08 PM / April 10, 2026 Artemis II crew back on Earth'; R2: 'splashed down... on Friday night, April 10'; R3: 'SPLASHDOWN!... April 10'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly state splashdown and mission conclusion on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule has splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported across multiple sources with exact location and splashdown confirmation.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed around 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R2: 'touched down at 5.07pm'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time matches in PDT/EDT across sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed approximately 40 to 50 miles offshore.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'about 50 miles offshore'
verifications.reasoning: Precise distance directly stated in references.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day trip to the moon'; R2: 'officially as a 10-day mission'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as 10-day crewed lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: US Navy vessels and specialized teams were positioned for retrieval near San Diego, as noted in the CNN live report and cbs8.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4 (cbs8.com): 'USS John P. Murtha... recover... off the coast of San Diego'; R8 (CNN): 'recovery ship, the USS John P. Murtha... off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: R4 and R8 directly note Navy vessels/teams near San Diego; others confirm.

verifications.claim: The reentry caused a sonic boom.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources predict possible sonic boom (e.g., R5), but none confirm it occurred during reentry.

verifications.claim: The landing was too far offshore for clear public viewing.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'not much from here, unfortunately... 50 miles offshore'; R9: 'difficult for people to see from land'
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate distance makes clear viewing difficult, but R4 suggests possible sighting from coast.

verifications.claim: The crew and capsule were transported back to Naval Air Station North Island in Coronado, California, for post-landing evaluations.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Naval Air Station North Island... recover the four astronauts'; R9: 'astronauts will be taken to Naval Air Station North Island... Naval Base Coronado'; R1: 'returned to Naval Base San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Crew helicopters from NAS North Island to ship for evaluations; capsule to Naval Base San Diego (includes North Island); not explicitly both to North Island for evaluations.
